title: Personality Disorder Continuum
summary: Move six dimensions of a fictional profile and draw a category line across them two different ways. Nothing here returns a diagnosis, and nothing is asked about you.
learningObjectives: Explain why unusual traits alone are not sufficient for a disorder-level interpretation.
Show that identical trait levels can be accompanied by very different impairment.
Distinguish subjective distress from functional impairment and say why both matter for different reasons.
Describe what changes when a continuum is cut into a category, and what does not.
State what a comprehensive professional assessment covers that six numbers cannot.
interactionTypes: threshold manipulation over a fictional population
privacy: No data collected, stored or transmitted; everything runs in the browser tab. The tool is not a self-test: it asks nothing about the person using it, produces no score for them, and returns no diagnosis for any profile.
accessibilityNotes: Native ranges, radios, checkboxes and buttons throughout; every slider announces what it controls in words and in bands ('rigidity low - whether the pattern can flex when a situation calls for something else') rather than as a bare number. Both charts are hidden from assistive technology and paired with visible tables: the dimensional profile table gives every value and its band, and gains a second column when the comparison profile is shown; the categorical table states which side of the line the profile falls on under each rule and what proportion of the fictional population falls above it. The category line is dashed and the profile is marked with a cross, so neither depends on colour. Judged selections open with the words 'Belongs in the answer' or 'Does not belong'. A content note appears before any interaction. Reduced motion honoured; forced-colours rules provided; usable at 320px and at classroom-projector widths.
readmeTopic: Personality pathology as a continuum: why unusual traits are not sufficient, and what changes when a category line is drawn
simulationNotes: Entirely fictional. There is no case study, no character and no named condition, and no diagnostic interview, criterion set, checklist, item or published questionnaire is reproduced, quoted or paraphrased. All six dimensions are set by the student and none is computed from any other, so the tool cannot imply that unusual traits produce impairment. One composite is calculated for the categorical view only - 0.30 rigidity plus 0.25 cross-situational persistence plus 0.25 functional impairment plus 0.20 interpersonal impact - with weights chosen for teaching rather than estimated from anything, and with subjective distress deliberately excluded so that distress and impairment stay distinguishable. The 800 fictional profiles behind the categorical view are generated once from a documented seed, with trait extremity normal with mean 50 and standard deviation 18 and functioning difficulty normal with mean 28 and standard deviation 16, correlated at about .55 and clipped to the 0 to 100 scale; the percentages counted from them exist to make the arithmetic of cut-offs visible and are not prevalence estimates. The tool returns no diagnosis under any setting.
